newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads narrow in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads narrow in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities narrowed to Treasuries in lighter-than-expected trading on Monday, market experts said.
Mortgages declined about 1/32 to 6/32 overall, while comparable Treasuries slipped 2/32 to 7/32.
Broadly based buying supported pass-through prices, traders said. Ginnie Mae 8.0s appeared to be the hot coupon, but "other than that it's been pretty quiet," one said.
Although they had expected a busier marketplace on Monday, traders said a pickup is not likely before Friday's jobs data.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were 5/32 lower at 99-23/32, yielding 107 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was also off 5/32, at 99-21/32, while Freddie Mac 7.5s had slipped 6/32 to 99-25/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 7/32 at 99-24/32, yielding 6.53 percent.

On Friday, the Labor Department will release employment data for December. Payrolls are expected to be up about 190,000, with the unemployment rate inching down to 5.3 percent, economists in a Reuters poll said Friday.
